artworks.title: American Stories from Sargent to O’Keeffe
artworks.description: More than 40 masterworks of American art lent by The Newark Museum of Art, in four sections (Identity, Belonging, Belief and Making), each opened by a question for visitors: paintings by John Singer Sargent, Albert Bierstadt, Edward Hopper and Georgia O’Keeffe, sculpture by Alexander Calder, Louise Nevelson and Martin Puryear, and Mickalene Thomas. Curated by Margarita Karasoulas. Included with admission.
artworks.galleryName: Changing Art Gallery (about 4,500 sq ft, William L. Richter Art Wing)
artworks.placeNote: Which gallery the show is in is a guess: the largest gallery for changing art shows.

artworks.title: Dustin Yellin: Politics of Eternity
artworks.description: An exhibition organized by the American Federation of Arts around Politics of Eternity (2020), an installation of glass about eleven feet long and nearly 11,000 pounds, with thousands of cut-out images sealed between its layers; excerpts of Yellin’s short film Goodnight, Lamby play nearby. Organized at the Bruce by Jordan Hillman, Assistant Curator of Art.
artworks.placeNote: Which gallery the show is in is a guess.

artworks.title: Rohini Devasher: Solar Poetics
artworks.description: The artist’s first solo museum show in the United States, built around One Hundred Thousand Suns (2023), a four-channel video new to the Bruce’s collection, drawn from the Kodaikanal Solar Observatory in India and its archive of about 157,000 portraits of the sun; with her works on copper. Closes November 29, 2026.
artworks.placeNote: Which gallery the show is in is a guess.

artworks.title: A Great Breach in Nature: Aerial Photography by J Henry Fair
artworks.description: Aerial photographs of industrial damage to the land and water, from Fair’s series Industrial Scars: art that explains science.
artworks.placeNote: The Changing Science Gallery, as the museum’s own floor plan names it.

artworks.title: Robert R. Wiener Mineral Gallery
artworks.description: About 200 minerals, most of them given by Robert R. Wiener: large crystals from around the world, a meteorite you can touch and minerals that glow under black light.
artworks.galleryName: Robert R. Wiener Mineral Gallery (about 200 minerals)
artworks.placeNote: Between the Sculpture Gallery and the changing science gallery, as the museum describes it; its exact rooms are approximate.
artworks.imageCredit: photo of the mineral cases before the 2023 rebuilding, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: Natural Cycles Shape Our Land
artworks.description: The Bruce’s permanent science exhibition: geology, fossils, archaeology and the Native peoples of the area, how Greenwich’s land and shore changed from before the settlers to the 1900s, a woodland diorama with local wildlife and birds, and a marine tank with small fish, crabs and sea stars.
artworks.galleryName: Permanent Science Galleries: Natural Cycles Shape Our Land
artworks.placeNote: The Permanent Science Galleries, as the museum’s own floor plan names them.
artworks.imageCredit: photo of the bird cases before the 2023 rebuilding, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: The Sculpture Gallery
artworks.description: The light-filled gallery that joins the William L. Richter Art Wing to the science wing, with views of Greenwich Harbor and Long Island Sound. The Bruce’s sculpture runs from Auguste Rodin, Hiram Powers and Frederick MacMonnies to George Segal.
artworks.galleryName: Sculpture Gallery: the link between the art and science wings, with views of Greenwich Harbor and Long Island Sound
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plans and the museum’s descriptions put it.

artworks.title: The new Bruce: lobby and main stairs
artworks.description: EskewDumezRipple’s 2023 wing put the lobby, café, store and lecture hall at the level of Bruce Park, 25 feet below the galleries; the stairs climb past the rock outcrop the building is set into. The whole ground floor is free during museum hours.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plans and the museum’s descriptions put it.
